answer: An agent earns an identity only by claiming a fresh vertex on a hardware graph: it must present a serialized ferrous tag, an iron-core module whose measured magnetization curve is posted on-chain, so forging a duplicate costs a foundry run rather than a loop iteration. Reputation then accrues like a sonnet, each line countersigned by the one before, and any colliding tag collapses both claimants back to zero weight.
